Author: Sunil Kumar Awasthi

THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH:BENCH AT INDORE  Cr.R. No. 3468/2018  (Kamal Das Vs. State of M.P. )
Indore, Dated:16/01/2020  Shri A.K. Saraswat, learned counsel for the applicant.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH:BENCH AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Gaurav Kumar Verma, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State.

ORDER The applicant has preferred the present revision petition under Section 397/401 of the Cr.P.C.
against judgment dated 18/07/2018 passed by Fourth Additional Sessions Judge, District-Dewas passed in Criminal Appeal No. 3800332/2016, whereby affirming the judgment dated 04/10/2016 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate, District-Dewas in Criminal Case No. 3159/2009, the applicant has been convicted for commission of offence punishable under Sections 7(I) and 7(II) read with Section 16(1)(A)(I) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to undergo RI for 6 months and to pay fine of Rs.1000/- for each offence with usual default stipulation.
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 10/04/2009 at about 4:30 p.m., Food Inspector, Dewas-Sushma Pathrod has inspected the shop of the applicant situated at 2/3 Bherugarh, Bada Bazar, Dewas and found that the applicant has manufacutred and sold the ice candy namedly Fruti Pepsi.

She has taken the samples of the ice candy and one of the sample was forwarded to State Food Laboratory,
Bhopal for examination.
The Public Analyst, vide report dated 21/10/2009 found that the said ice candy was adulterated.

On the receipt of the said report, Food Inspector- Sushma Pathrod, Dewas has made a request to the competent authority/CMO, Dewas for written consent for launching the prosecution against the applicant and the said permission was granted to the Food Inspector by the CMO, Dewas on 24/10/2009.

Thereafter, Food Inspector sent a notice to the applicant under Section 13(2) of the PFA Act and then, she filed the complaint against the applicant for commission of offence punishable under Sections Sections 7(I) and 7(II) read with Section 16(1)(A)(I) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

3. The trial court by adopting the summons procedure, read over the particular of offence to the applicant for commission of offence punishable under Sections 7(I) and 7(II) read with Section 16(1)(A)(I) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
The applicant abjured his guilt and pleaded innocence, however, he has not examined any witness in his defence.

sentences.text:
After recording the evidence of the parties, the trial Court while passing the impugned judgment,
convicted and sentenced the applicant for the commission of offence as mentioned herein above.

The said judgment of conviction was challenged by the applicant before the Sessions Court by filing Criminal Appeal No. 3800332/2016, which got dismissed by the Fourth Additional Sessions Judge,
District-Dewas by affirming the judgment of the trial Court, therefore, the applicant has preferred the present revision petition before this Court.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the independent witnesses of the case did not support the prosecution story and turned hostile.

As per the statement of Sushma Patharol (PW 1),
she never gives any notice under Sction 13(2) of the PFA Act to the applicant and no dispatch of the said notice has been filed, therefore, the applicant is deprived from his valuable right, which has been conferred upon him for sending the second sample of the said food article to Central Food Laboraty for chemical analysis.
Hence, the trial court as well as appellate Court have committed error in convicting the applicant for the aforesaid offence.
Under these circumstances, learned counsel for the applicant prays for setting aside of the impugned judgments and acquittal of the applicant.

6. On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor supported the impugned judgments by contending that all the necessary compliance has been made before launcing the prosecution against the applicant and there is no ground available on record to interfere the concurrents findings recorded by the courts' below.

Under these circumstances, he prayed for dismissal of the revision petition.
7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.

8. From the statement of Sushma Patharol, Food Inspector, Dewas (PW 1), it appears that on on 10/04/2009, she was posted as Food Inspector, Dewas and on the aforesaid date, at about 4:30 p.m., she has inspected the shop of the applicant situated at 2/3 Bherugarh, Bada Bazar, Dewas and found that the applicant has manufacutred and sold the ice candy namedly Fruti Pepsi.
When the license was asked from the applicant, he failed to produce the same.
Then she has taken the samples of the ice cany and one of the sample was forwarded to State Food Laboratory, Bhopal for examination.
According to the report dated 21/10/2009, of the Public Analyst the said ice candy was found adulterated.

On the receipt of the said report, Food Inspector-Sushma Pathrod, Dewas has made a request to the competent authority/CMO, Dewas for written consent for launching the prosecution against the applicant and the said permission (Ex. P/7) was granted to the Food Inspector by the CMO, Dewas on 24/10/2009.

She also deposed in her statement that after taking the prosecution sanction from CMO, Dewas, she sent a notice to the applicant under Section 13(2) of the PFA Act by registered AD mode and according to acknowledgement (Ex. P/19), the notice was received by the applicant, therefore, the submission made by the learned counsel for the applicant is not acceptable that the prosecution has not complied with provision of Section 13(2) of the PFA Act,
hence, the applicant is deprived from his valuable right to apply for sending the second sample of the said food article to Central Food Laboratory for examination.

Though, Madhubala (PW 2) did not support the prosecution story and turned hostile, however, from the minute scrutiny of evidence of Sushma Patharol (PW 1), this Court is of the considered view that the courts' below have not committed any error in convicting the applicant for commission of offence punishable under Kamal Das vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145783204/
2 Sections 7(I) and 7(II) read with Section 16(1)(A)(I) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
9.

sentences.text: It is also pertinent to note that the revisional jurisdiction of the court is very limited and reappreciation of the prosecution is not required and no intereference in the impugned judgements is called for, therefore, the conviction recorded by the courts below is hereby affirmed.
10. So far as the question of sentence is concerned, the applicant is aged about 58 years, he is not having any criminal antecedents and he is the only earning member of his family.

But the applicant has been convicted for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 7(I) and 7(II) read with Section 16(1)(A)(I) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, in which minimum sentence of 6 months RI is prescribed, therefore, no case for reducing the custodial sentence of the applicant is made out.

11. In view of the foregoing discussion, this court is of the opinion that no case for the interference in the impugned judgments is called for, therefore, by affirming the conviction and sentence of the applicant, the present revision petition is hereby dismissed.
The applicant is on bail, therefore, his bail bonds stands cancelled and he is directed to surrender immediately before the trial Court for serving out remaining jail sentence.
12. Let a copy of this court alongwith the records be sent to the concerned courts' below for information.

(S. K. Awasthi)
